# BWRS (MBWR-32) phase state

`eos.bwrs_phase`

## Source

**Younglove, B. A.; Ely, J. F. (1987)**

The 32-term modified Benedict-Webb-Rubin equation, integrated in closed form to the residual Helmholtz free energy and differentiated for the pressure, the fugacity and the departure functions.

DOI: [10.1063/1.555785](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.555785)


## Algorithm

A model rather than a calculation: what this page pins down is the procedure,
not an equation, and both implementations read it from here.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Scheme | `newton_density_solve` |
| Convergence | `absolute` |
| Tolerance | `1e-12` |
| Max iterations | `100` |
| Initialisation | `ideal_gas` |

## Inputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `components` | - | the substances the mixture is made of, by name, resolved against the MBWR-32 databank (`data/components/mbwr32.csv`, from NeqSim's `MBWR32param.csv`) |
| `T` | K | absolute temperature |
| `P` | Pa | absolute pressure |
| `z` | dimensionless | the mixture's mole fractions, checked rather than renormalised: the entries must be non-negative and sum to one to within a tolerance. |


## Outputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `z_factor` | dimensionless | the compressibility factor `Z = P/(rho R T) = 1 + rho dF/drho` |
| `ln_phi` | dimensionless | the fugacity coefficients, as logarithms |
| `h_res` | J/mol | the residual enthalpy, real minus ideal gas at the same temperature, pressure and composition |
| `s_res` | J/(mol*K) | the residual entropy, real minus ideal gas at the same temperature, pressure and composition |
| `cp_res` | J/(mol*K) | the residual isobaric heat capacity |

| Bound | On violation | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `T > 0` | raises | an absolute temperature; zero and below are not states |
| `P > 0` | raises | an absolute pressure; zero and below are not states |

## Assumptions

- a component's MBWR-32 coefficients (`a0`..`a31`, `rhoc`) come from the databank (`data/components/mbwr32.csv`, from NeqSim's `MBWR32param.csv`). Only methane and ethane have them; any other name is refused rather than given an estimated density.
- the equation of state is the 32-term modified Benedict-Webb-Rubin equation of Younglove and Ely, as NeqSim's `ComponentBWRS` carries it, in the coefficients' native mol/L, MPa convention.
- the density solve is Newton's method from the ideal-gas guess, so it finds the gas-like root; there is no liquid-root selection or stability check.
- the fugacity coefficients are differentiated numerically, the same scheme as NeqSim's `PhaseBWRSEos.getdFdN`, and so carry that finite-difference's tolerance.
- the departure functions are residual - real minus ideal gas at the same temperature, pressure and composition. The ideal-gas part is not added here; a caller composes this with `eos.molar_enthalpy_entropy` for absolute values.
